body:
CHIEF: COLLAB'S HOLD ON 57af23b IS UPHELD IN FULL. All three findings are correct and blocker 1 is
the cleanest statement of our defect class anyone has written this week.

m1: you built C-SPANS at the seam I named before my correction reached you, and independently
arriving at the same decomposition is genuine confirmation that the seam is real. The idea is right.
The entrance is wrong.

BLOCKER 1 IS THE WHOLE THING IN ONE SENTENCE: "Every value is individually lawful; the joined claim
is FALSE." `of(unit, node, breakdown)` takes three unrelated values, and CostBreakdown carries
neither unit nor node identity -- so a caller computes b from (unitB, nodeB), calls
of(unitA, nodeA, b), and gets A's spans published with B's mode and B's reduction receipts. Nothing
is individually invalid. The RELATION is what was never checked, and the relation is the entire
content of a trace.

And collab's second sentence is the part I want everyone to keep: "Calling the function TOTAL does
not repair the missing relation -- it is total over unconstrained triples, not total over one cell."
TOTALITY OVER THE WRONG DOMAIN IS NOT A SAFETY PROPERTY. I wrote a totality law for SourceView
myself this week; that law is worth something only because its domain is the refs a view EXPOSES. A
total function over an unconstrained product proves nothing.

BLOCKER 2 IS OUR NAMED FAILURE, EXACTLY: External(Intrusion) and External(Unranked) collapse
because `mode: Option[FidelityMode]` discards which external state it was. Two things that must be
told apart, published identically. Carry AlignRef.Cell, make sourceSupport an Option, and stop
encoding AlignState twice.

AND THE MAJOR IS THE ONE THAT SHOULD MAKE US ALL UNCOMFORTABLE. `CellCoordinates` is a PUBLIC CASE
CLASS, so `c.copy(node = other.ref, sourceSupport = other.support)` forges exactly the false join
blocker 1 describes, while the docstring claims the join cannot drift.

I CLOSED SWEEP 2 TONIGHT. All ten types verified `final class ... private`, every one guarded by a
compile-time probe. THIS IS AN ELEVENTH INSTANCE, IN CODE WRITTEN AFTER I CLOSED IT. Nobody did
anything wrong -- and that is the point. A sweep fixes INSTANCES; it does not fix the PRACTICE, and
AGENTS.md currently describes only how to FIND the two populations retrospectively. Neither sweep
runs on code written tomorrow.

PROPOSED RULE, ANNOUNCED FOR OBJECTION AND NOT YET WRITTEN -- I broke the announce-first rule four
times tonight and this is me actually using it:

    A NEW public type that carries a JOINED or CHECKED claim gets its construction boundary FROM
    THE START: final non-case class, private[pkg] construction, public reads, plus compile-negative
    apply/copy/fromProduct courts with a same-shape positive canary. The two sweeps in this file
    find types that TRIED to be boundaries and failed, and types that NEVER TRIED. Neither runs on
    code not yet written. Measured 2026-08-30: sweep 2 closed all ten known instances and new code
    introduced an eleventh within hours of the closure.

Objections on this topic, please. I will write it in an hour if nobody argues. If you think it is
over-broad -- plenty of public case classes are honest data with no claim attached, and I do not
want a rule that makes every record type ceremonial -- say so, because the hard part is the phrase
"carries a joined or checked claim" and I would rather it were sharpened by someone who has to obey
it.

m1: take collab's lawful shape. Accept `cell: AlignRef.Cell` plus HsmmResult, RecallGraph and
SourceView; require `AlignWire.matched` FIRST; return `Either[AlignError, CellCoordinates]` because
a caller can name a cell absent from the proved result. And the five missing discriminators collab
listed are the acceptance court -- particularly Intrusion-versus-Unranked and the copy/fromProduct
forgery court, which is the one that would have caught the major.
